options: A table with a single Date column containing every date between the two dates, inclusive
A single scalar date value

questions.explain: CALENDAR builds a contiguous run of dates, one row per day, from start_date through end_date — exactly the shape a date table needs.

questions.q: Why is CALENDAR(MINX(Sales, [Date]), MAXX(Forecast, [Date])) more robust than a hardcoded date range?
options: It automatically adjusts as new rows are added to Sales or Forecast, instead of silently going stale
It runs faster than a fixed date range in every case
It only works with DirectQuery data sources
It removes the need for a Year column
questions.explain: A hardcoded range doesn't expand when new data arrives. Deriving the range from MINX/MAXX keeps the calendar automatically in sync with the actual data.

questions.q: What does CALENDARAUTO do differently from CALENDAR?
options: It scans every date column in the entire model and builds a calendar spanning all of them, rounded to complete fiscal years
It requires you to manually specify a start and end date
It only works on a single table, not the whole model
It removes the need for a date table entirely
questions.explain: CALENDARAUTO needs no explicit range — it finds the earliest and latest dates anywhere in the model automatically and rounds to full fiscal years.

questions.q: What kind of table does CALENDAR or CALENDARAUTO create in Power BI Desktop?
options: A calculated table, created via New Table
A calculated column added to an existing table
A measure
A Power Query custom column
questions.explain: Both functions return a table, so they're entered as a calculated table (New Table) — a table whose rows come from a DAX formula rather than imported data.

questions.q: Why isn't a bare Date column from CALENDAR immediately a fully useful date table?
options: It typically still needs additional calculated columns like Year, Quarter, and Month before it's marked as the date table and used for hierarchies
CALENDAR output can never be marked as a date table
It needs to be converted into a measure first
It must be manually sorted before use
questions.explain: A single Date column satisfies the date-table validation rules, but most models add Year/Quarter/Month columns on top before building real hierarchies from it.
